title: Niger Votes Yes in French Constitutional Referendum
note: Confirmed: Niger voted yes (78%) in the 28 September 1958 referendum on de Gaulle's constitution, opting for the French Community. PPN under Diori did support the yes vote. Event year, country, and core claim all match.

title: Niger Independence and Hamani Diori Presidency
note: Confirmed: Niger gained independence on August 3, 1960; Diori became first president (elected by National Assembly in November 1960). Description correctly calls him first president and notes single-party PPN rule and pro-French foreign policy.

title: Nigerien Opposition Parties Banned
note: The main opposition (Sawaba) was actually banned in 1959, before independence. After independence PPN maintained a de facto single-party state, but the specific framing of a 1961 dissolution decree is not confirmed. The year is likely off — the consolidation happened at/before independence in 1960, not 1961. Cannot mark VERIFIED but cannot confirm as outright FALSE without more precise sourcing.

title: Niger Joins OCAM and Deepens Francophone Ties
note: WRONG YEAR. OCAM (Organisation Commune Africaine et Malgache) was set up in February 1965 at Nouakchott, not 1963. Niger was a founding member of its predecessor UAM (1961) and then OCAM (1965). The event description fits 1965, not 1963.

title: Uranium Discovered in Arlit Region
note: WRONG YEAR AND CLAIM. Uranium was first discovered in Niger in 1957 (Azelik). Deposits near Arlit (Arlette/Arlit) were found around 1965. SOMAIR was formed in 1968, marking the decision to mine — not the discovery. The claim that major deposits were 'confirmed in 1968' conflates discovery with corporate setup.

title: Arlit Uranium Mine Opens
note: Confirmed: SOMAIR began commercial production from the Arlit deposit in 1971. COGEMA (later AREVA) was a key partner. Year, country, and core claim all match.

title: Sahel Famine Devastates Niger
note: Confirmed: The Sahel drought-famine of 1968-1974 killed approximately 100,000 people; the 1973-1974 peak was catastrophic. Diori government was criticized for mishandling food aid. Claim of ~100,000 deaths and food aid diversion controversy are well documented.

title: Kountche Military Coup Ousts Diori
note: Confirmed: Kountche led coup on April 15, 1974; Diori placed under house arrest (died 1989). Constitution suspended, National Assembly dissolved, Supreme Military Council established. All details match.

title: Kountche Renegotiates Uranium Contracts with France
note: Uranium renegotiations under Kountche are documented in general terms (tensions over pricing existed). However, a specific 1975 renegotiation with a formal outcome is not confirmed by available sources. The broader pattern is accurate but the specific year and outcome are unverifiable from available sources.

title: Development Society (Societe de Developpement) National Framework Launched
note: Confirmed: Kountche's 'Société de Développement' project is documented. Sources confirm it was launched as a grassroots consultative framework without restoring multiparty politics, funded by uranium revenues. Year circa 1979-1980 is consistent.

title: Uranium Price Collapse Triggers Economic Crisis
note: Confirmed: Global uranium prices collapsed in the mid-1980s (beginning early 1980s after Three Mile Island 1979). Uranium's share of government revenue fell from 40% to 12% by 1986. IMF structural adjustment followed. Year 1983 is slightly early — the collapse deepened from 1985 onward — but the onset of the crisis in the early 1980s is supported.

title: President Kountche Dies; Ali Saibou Succeeds
note: Confirmed: Kountche died November 10, 1987 (brain tumor, Paris hospital). Ali Saibou succeeded him as head of Supreme Military Council on November 14, 1987. All details match.

title: New Constitution Approved Under Saibou
note: Confirmed: Constitutional referendum held September 24, 1989; MNSD established as sole legal party. Saibou formalized as president unopposed. Event year, country, and core claim match.

title: Pro-Democracy Protests Erupt
note: Confirmed: February 9, 1990 — security forces killed several students during pro-democracy demonstrations in Niamey. The 'massacre of 9 February' became a landmark event. Government made concessions on political openness. Event year, country, and core claim match.

title: First Tuareg Insurgency Begins in Northern Niger
note: Confirmed: In May 1990, Tuareg attacked a police station in Tchin-Tabaradene; Nigerien military response killed hundreds of civilians. Libya-trained fighters involved. Insurgency in Agadez/Air region confirmed for 1990. All key claims match.

title: Sovereign National Conference Opens Multiparty Transition
note: Confirmed: National Sovereign Conference opened July 29, 1991; stripped Saibou of executive power; Amadou Cheiffou appointed transitional PM; High Council of Republic established as interim legislature. All details match.

title: New Multiparty Constitution Approved
note: Confirmed: Constitutional referendum held December 26, 1992; approved by 89.79%; established semi-presidential multiparty system; Third Republic proclaimed January 22, 1993. All details match.

title: Mahamane Ousmane Wins First Free Presidential Election
note: Confirmed: Ousmane of CDS won in second round on March 27, 1993, defeating Tandja of MNSD. First multi-candidate presidential election since independence. International observers declared it free and fair.

title: Ousmane Government Faces Cohabitation Crisis
note: Confirmed: Issoufou resigned as PM on September 28, 1994 after Ousmane strengthened presidential powers. Parliamentary elections in January 1995 produced MNSD-PNDS opposition majority. Hama Amadou became PM, not Issoufou. Note: the event text incorrectly says Issoufou became PM in cohabitation — he resigned in 1994; Hama Amadou (MNSD) was the cohabitation PM.

title: Tuareg Peace Accord Signed in Ouagadougou
note: Confirmed: Peace accord signed April 1995 in Ouagadougou between Niger government and Tuareg ORA, mediated by Algeria, Burkina Faso, and France. Ended the 1990-1995 insurgency. All key details match.

title: Ibrahim Bare Mainassara Leads Military Coup
note: Confirmed: Mainassara led coup on January 27, 1996, overthrowing Ousmane. Constitution suspended, National Salvation Council formed. Hama Amadou arrested. All details match.

title: Mainassara Wins Disputed Presidential Election
note: Confirmed: Presidential election July 7-8, 1996. Mainassara dissolved independent electoral commission (CENI) mid-count on day two and replaced it with loyalist body (CNE). Won with ~52%. Western donors suspended aid. All details match.

title: Mainassara Assassinated; Wanke Takes Power
note: Confirmed: Mainassara killed on April 9, 1999 at Niamey airport by Presidential Guard. Daouda Malam Wanke assumed power via National Reconciliation Council. All details match.

title: New Constitution Approved; Mamadou Tandja Elected President
note: Confirmed: Constitution approved July 18, 1999 (Fifth Republic). Tandja won presidential election second round in November 1999; sworn in December 22, 1999. All details match.

title: Military Mutinies in Niamey and Diffa
note: Confirmed: Mutiny began July 30, 2002 in Diffa; spread to Niamey (suppressed August 5); soldiers demanded better pay and conditions; government negotiated resolution. Two soldiers killed. All key details match.

title: Locust Plague and Drought Cause Widespread Food Crisis
note: Confirmed: Worst locust invasion in 15 years hit Niger in August-October 2004; combined with drought; 3.6 million people affected; crisis peaked in 2005. International aid response criticized as slow. All key details match.

title: Tandja Re-elected for Second Term
note: Confirmed: Tandja won second term in second-round runoff on December 4, 2004, defeating Issoufou (65.53% vs 34.47%). Sworn in December 21, 2004. Election declared free and fair by international observers. All details match.

title: Second Tuareg Rebellion Led by MNJ
note: Confirmed: MNJ (Mouvement des Nigeriens pour la Justice) launched rebellion starting February 8, 2007, attacking military patrols and AREVA uranium facilities. Demanded greater revenue share and 1995 accord implementation. All key details match.

title: Niger Signs Major Uranium Deal with China
note: Confirmed: SOMINA joint venture (CNNC International 37.2%) incorporated June 2007 with mining license November 2007 for Azelik; construction began July 2008. The deal was signed in 2007-2008. Event year of 2008 is consistent with construction start and formal agreement signing.

title: Tandja Pushes Through Controversial Constitutional Referendum
note: Confirmed: Referendum held August 4, 2009; abolished presidential term limits and extended Tandja's rule by three years. Constitutional Court ruled against it on May 25 and June 20, 2009; Tandja dissolved the court. All details match.

title: ECOWAS and African Union Condemn Tandja
note: Confirmed: ECOWAS suspended Niger in October 2009; EU suspended budget support. African Union expressed condemnation. All core details match. Note: the AU suspension of Niger from all activities was formally enacted after the February 2010 coup, not in 2009; the 2009 AU response was condemnation/concern rather than formal suspension.

title: Military Coup Overthrows Tandja; CSRD Takes Power
note: Confirmed: Coup on February 18, 2010; Tandja arrested during cabinet meeting; CSRD (Supreme Council for the Restoration of Democracy) led by Colonel Salou Djibo. Constitution suspended, state institutions dissolved. All details match.

title: Mahamadou Issoufou Wins Presidential Election
note: Confirmed: Issoufou of PNDS won second round on March 12, 2011 with ~58% of vote. Welcomed by international observers as Niger's first democratic transfer of power. All details match.

title: Mali Crisis Sends Refugees and Armed Groups into Niger
note: Confirmed: 2012 Mali crisis sent refugees and armed factions toward Niger. French Operation Serval launched January 2013 (not 2012) pushed jihadists toward Niger. Niger became frontline state. Minor note: Operation Serval was a 2013 response to the 2012 crisis, so the event's claim about Niger hosting Serval logistics in 2012 is slightly off — the logistics support role solidified in early 2013.

title: AREVA Contract Dispute Over Uranium Pricing
note: Confirmed: Niger engaged in protracted negotiations with AREVA over royalties from 2013-2014 demanding increase from 5.5% to 12%. Dispute over pricing formula and revenue share. All key details match.

title: Suicide Bombings Target Arlit Mine and Military Base
note: Confirmed: Twin suicide bombings on May 23, 2013 hit AREVA's Somair uranium mine in Arlit and military barracks in Agadez. Total killed approximately 20-26. MUJAO claimed responsibility (with Belmokhtar/AQIM connection). Event says 25 killed — close to confirmed count. All key details match.

title: Niger Joins G5 Sahel Security Framework
note: Confirmed: G5 Sahel created February 16, 2014 in Nouakchott; Niger was a founding member alongside Burkina Faso, Chad, Mali, Mauritania. Convention adopted December 19, 2014. All details match.

title: Boko Haram Attacks Across Lake Chad Region
note: Confirmed: Boko Haram's first major incursion into Niger's Diffa region occurred February 6, 2015; over 70 attacks in Diffa during 2015; 129,000+ internally displaced plus 108,000 Nigerian refugees. All key details match.

title: Charlie Hebdo Protests Turn Violent in Zinder and Niamey
note: Confirmed: January 2015 protests over Charlie Hebdo cartoons resulted in 10 deaths, dozens of churches burned (at least 45 churches), and widespread destruction in Zinder and Niamey. All key details match.

title: US Drone Base Established at Agadez
note: PARTIAL: US military presence at Air Base 201 began April 19, 2016 (not 2015). Congressional notification and agreement were in 2014-2015, construction began summer 2016. Calling the establishment 2015 is premature — operations began 2016. The event year is off by at least one year.

title: Issoufou Re-elected in Second Term
note: Confirmed: Issoufou won second round on March 20, 2016 with 92.5% after opposition boycott. First round February 21, 2016 gave him ~48%. All key details match.

title: Four US Special Forces Soldiers Killed in Tongo Tongo Ambush
note: Confirmed: October 4, 2017 ambush near Tongo Tongo; 4 US soldiers and 4 Nigerien soldiers killed; ISGS responsible (AQIM affiliation). Congressional investigation followed. All details match.

title: AREVA Renamed Orano; New Uranium Contract Signed
note: WRONG YEAR FOR REBRANDING. AREVA officially renamed Orano on January 23, 2018, not 2017. The restructuring was announced in 2017 but the rebrand took effect in January 2018. The event is filed under 2017 but the renaming is a 2018 fact.

title: Islamic State Greater Sahara Escalates Attacks in Tillaberi
note: Confirmed: ISGS dramatically intensified attacks in Tillaberi in 2019-2020; December 2019 Inates attack killed 70+ soldiers; January 2020 Chinagodrar attack killed 89 soldiers. Mass displacement occurred. All key details match.

title: Mohamed Bazoum Wins Presidential Election
note: Confirmed: Bazoum of PNDS won February 2021 second-round runoff with 55.7% defeating Mahamane Ousmane. Niger's first peaceful transfer of power between elected presidents. All details match.

title: Coup Attempt Foiled on Eve of Bazoum Inauguration
note: Confirmed: Coup attempt night of March 30-31, 2021 (day before inauguration April 1; sworn in April 2). Forces from nearby air base attacked presidential palace; presidential guard repelled attack. Several arrested. All details match.

title: Massacre at Tillaberi Villages Kills Over 100 Civilians
note: Confirmed: March 21, 2021 ISGS attack on villages near Tillia (Tahoua Region) killed 137+ civilians. Described as deadliest jihadist attack in Niger's history. Note: the attack was in Tahoua Region (Tillia), not Tillaberi Region. The event title says Tillaberi — this is a region error, though both regions border Mali.

title: Niger Signs New Military Cooperation Accord with France
note: Niger's role as France's Sahel partner deepened in 2022 after Mali expelled French forces. However, a specific new signed military cooperation framework in 2022 is not confirmed — existing 2013 agreements remained in force. The claim of a new accord signed in 2022 is not substantiated; the existing SOFA/cooperation framework was carried over rather than a fresh signing.

title: Niger Becomes Key Transit for European Migration Policy
note: Confirmed: Niger was central to EU-funded migration containment (Law 36-2015 criminalizing migration; EU Action Plan); Niger received €294 million by December 2022 (largest Sahel recipient). Human rights abuses by Nigerien security forces under EU contracts documented. All key details match.

title: Military Coup Overthrows President Bazoum
note: Confirmed: Presidential Guard commander General Abdourahamane Tchiani led coup on July 26, 2023; Bazoum detained; CNSP established. All details match.

title: ECOWAS Issues Ultimatum and Threatens Military Intervention
note: Confirmed: ECOWAS issued seven-day ultimatum July 30, 2023; junta rejected it; ECOWAS activated standby force; Niger closed airspace. Mali and Burkina juntas pledged support for Niger. All key details match.

title: France Expels Its Troops After Junta Revokes Military Agreement
note: Confirmed: Junta revoked defense agreements August 2023; France announced withdrawal September 2023; last French troops departed by December 22, 2023. Approximately 1,500 French troops withdrawn. All details match.

title: Niger, Mali, and Burkina Faso Form Alliance of Sahel States
note: Confirmed: Alliance of Sahel States (AES) mutual defense pact signed September 16, 2023 in response to ECOWAS intervention threat. All three junta-led states signed. All details match.

title: US Suspends Most Aid to Niger Following Coup
note: Confirmed: US formally designated coup on October 10, 2023; suspended approximately $500 million in aid (including $442 million MCC funding). US retained military presence at Agadez pending negotiations. All key details match.

title: Bazoum Held in Detention; International Release Demands Ignored
note: Confirmed: Bazoum remained in detention throughout 2023 and beyond; ECOWAS court, UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention, and multiple international bodies demanded his release; junta ignored all demands. All details match.

title: US Agadez Drone Base Eviction Ordered by Junta
note: Confirmed: Junta terminated SOFA on March 16, 2024 with immediate effect; US completed withdrawal from Air Base 101 (Niamey) July 7 and Air Base 201 (Agadez) August 5, 2024. Approximately 1,000 US troops withdrawn. All details match.

title: Russian Wagner Forces Arrive in Niger
note: Confirmed: Russian Africa Corps (Wagner successor) deployed to Niger; troops arrived April 12, 2024, training Nigerien forces including drone operations. Event correctly identifies Africa Corps as Wagner successor. All key details match.

title: Niger Announces Withdrawal from ECOWAS
note: Confirmed: Niger announced ECOWAS withdrawal January 28-30, 2024 alongside Mali and Burkina Faso. Formal exit completed January 29, 2025 after one-year notice period. All key details match.

title: Uranium Export Contracts Re-evaluated; Orano Operations Suspended
note: Confirmed: Niger revoked Imouraren mining license June 20-21, 2024; SOMAIR (Orano's Arlit operation) also faced suspension; government opened reviews of all extraction agreements. Orano initiated legal proceedings. All key details match.

title: AES States Sign Confederation Treaty
note: Confirmed: Niger, Mali, Burkina Faso signed confederation treaty July 6, 2024 at summit in Niamey; established formal confederation with shared institutions, rotating presidency, and goal of eventual federation. All key details match.

title: Niger Pipeline and Oil Exports Resume Amid Political Uncertainty
note: Confirmed: Niger-Benin pipeline (CNPC-built, 1,950km) began exports May 2024 after border dispute resolved; pipeline attacked June 2024 after first shipment; exports resumed August 2024. Niger's first oil export infrastructure. All key details match.
